output.title: Eval drift is a threshold question, not a slogan
output.body:
If you are automating one recurring workflow in a small business, eval drift is not abstract. It is the question of when you would stop trusting the system because real work has changed underneath it.

The useful move is to make that a workflow decision before you automate. Pick one process, such as inbox triage or invoice handling, and define the measurable outcome in plain language: what counts as correct, what gets sent to manual review, and what would trigger a pause. The percentages in that kind of rule are just an example, not a benchmark. The point is to set the threshold in advance.

That matters because human approval stays mandatory for money movement and other high-risk decisions. An AI system should not quietly keep going when the pattern changes. If confidence drops, the owner needs to see it and take back control.

A practical next step is simple: ask, “How will I know this system is drifting?” and “What decision still has to stay with me?” If you cannot answer those two questions, you do not yet have a bounded automation. You have a guess.
